observation.visible_scene: An outdoor metal fire pit / stove-like box, composed of a left section with curved decorative metal loops on its front face and a right section that is a plain box with a horizontal metal bar on its front. The top opening of the box is actively burning, producing orange-yellow flames and a thick white-grey smoke plume. The background is a blurred spring garden with green foliage, white blossoms, a tree trunk at the right edge and a dark building at the left. The metal object and the background remain fixed in frame position throughout, indicating a static camera.
visible_changes: Flames rising from the top of the box flicker and change shape continuously, being tall and bright in the early frames (1-4), receding and becoming patchy in the middle frames (20-30), and re-igniting into a more consolidated orange flame in the later frames (35-41).
A white-grey smoke plume billows upward and drifts leftward, growing denser and spreading wider over the course of the clip, increasingly enveloping the flames by the final frames.

The relative balance between fire and smoke shifts: early frames show dominant open flame on the right with smoke on the left, while later frames show heavier smoke on both sides with the flame partly obscured.
The metal box, its decorative loops, the horizontal bar, and the background elements do not move or deform; only the fire and smoke evolve.
The fire and smoke are already ongoing at the first frame and still active at the last frame; no ignition or extinguishing is captured within the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: What fuel or material is being burned is not visible.
When the fire started and whether it will continue or die out after the clip are unknown.
Any wind source driving the leftward smoke drift is not directly observable.
uncertain_details: Camera motion appears absent given the fixed background and object, but a very slight handheld jitter cannot be fully ruled out.

The exact height and intensity of the flame at each instant fluctuate too rapidly to assign a smooth monotonic trend; the description of 'receding then re-igniting' reflects frame-to-frame turbulence rather than a controlled change.
